_comment: Files with jsx-a11y/control-has-associated-label violations. eslint.config.js reads this list and downgrades the rule to a warning FOR THESE FILES ONLY, so a violation in any other file is an error and fails `npm run lint`. The list may only SHRINK: src/test/a11y_debt_is_accurate.test.ts fails if a listed file has no violations left (delete its entry) or if a listed file no longer exists. An entry that describes nothing is how a ratchet stops being one. F172.
_shape: The 138 measured on 2026-09-13 were described as 'icon-only buttons without an accessible name'. Classified with the same parser eslint uses, exactly ONE was a button: input 108, textarea 17, div 5, td 4, th 2, button 1, option 1. Sixteen more were false positives of a kind worth knowing about - a control carrying id="x" with a sibling <label htmlFor="x">, which is correctly labelled at runtime and unresolvable by a static rule. Clear those by giving the label an id and the control aria-labelledby, never by copying the text into an aria-label that can drift from what is on screen (WCAG 2.5.3). The remaining 121 are controls with no accessible name at all, and are real.
_triage:
CLEARED 2026-09-18 — 0 findings, 0 files. The list is empty and the rule is now an ERROR in every file with no exceptions, which is the state this ratchet existed to reach. eslint.config.js spreads the override block rather than stating it, because flat config rejects `files: []` at LOAD time and an empty list would otherwise take `npm run lint` down with it for every rule in that file.

History, kept because it is the reasoning: triaged one by one on 2026-09-15, because 'known limitation of one rule' is a label that hides a real defect. jsx-a11y/control-has-associated-label looks DOWN into a control's own children for text; it never looks UP at a wrapping <label>, and it does not follow htmlFor/id across that shape. Seventeen of the eighteen findings were therefore its blind spot and the code was already correct at runtime — e.g. <label>Start Date <input type="date"/></label> (ReplayPage), <label htmlFor={`journal-notes-${id}`}>Notes</label> with the matching <textarea id=...> (TradeJournal), a radio inside a <label> carrying the option text (FinancialSection), and a <td> inside an aria-hidden skeleton row (DataTable). The eighteenth was real and was fixed first: superadmin/ui.tsx's Toggle rendered div[role="switch"] inside a <label>, and a <label> implicitly labels only LABELABLE elements (input, select, textarea, button, meter, output, progress) — so all 64 uses announced as "switch, off" with no name, several of them controlling how the platform trades. See src/test/the_superadmin_toggle_has_a_name.test.tsx.

How the seventeen were cleared, and what was NOT done: the association was made EXPLICIT rather than duplicated. The element already rendering the visible text was given an id and the control an aria-labelledby, so there is still exactly one copy of the text and nothing to drift at the first rename (WCAG 2.5.3). aria-label was used in only three places, each one where no id could be pointed at: two where the name IS the same binding that renders the visible text (AIIntelligence's `{control}`, and the datalist <option>'s value in PlatformConfiguration, where a server-supplied string cannot safely be spliced into an id), and one where the wrapping text lives in settings/ui.tsx's `Field` whose `label` prop is a plain string with no element to reference. The DataTable <td> got no name at all, because a shimmer placeholder has none: its row was already aria-hidden, and the cell now restates that ancestor fact where a static rule can read it. No eslint-disable was used anywhere.

The rule going quiet and a screen reader getting a name are different claims. All six shapes above were rendered under @testing-library and queried by accessible name before this entry was emptied.
